article_title: The Effect of 7E Learning Cycle on Learning in Science Teaching: A Meta-Analysis Study
citation: Balta, N., & Sarac, H. (2016). The Effect of 7E Learning Cycle on Learning in Science Teaching: A meta-Analysis Study. European Journal of Educational Research, 5(2), 61-72. https://doi.org/10.12973/eu-jer.5.2.61
title: The 7E learning cycle: a seven-phase constructivist instructional model for science teaching
description: The 7E learning cycle is a constructivist, student-centered instructional model consisting of seven phases: "elicit, engage, explore, explain, elaborate, evaluate, and extend". It expands the 5E model by splitting engage into elicit and engage, emphasizing prior understanding and misconceptions, and by adding an extend phase so students "transfer their learning to a new context". Each phase has described activities: concept cartoons and demonstrations in elicit, discrepant events in engage, questioning and worksheets in explore, teacher explanation with concept maps in explain, application to new areas in elaborate, formative and summative evaluation in evaluate, and transfer to everyday life in extend.
requirements: Teachers carry out each phase; the article notes the model "can be time-consuming because of the fact that each phase should be carried out meticulously"
constraints: The article notes the model can be time-consuming when each phase is carried out meticulously
target_learning_goals: transfer of learning to new contexts
examples: The meta-analysis synthesized 24 primary studies that implemented the 7E cycle in biology, chemistry, physics and science courses across middle school, high school and university levels
key_sources: Balta, N., & Sarac, H. (2016). The Effect of 7E Learning Cycle on Learning in Science Teaching: A meta-Analysis Study. European Journal of Educational Research, 5(2), 61-72. https://doi.org/10.12973/eu-jer.5.2.61

article_title: Effects of 7E Learning Cycle Model and Case-Based Learning Strategy on Secondary School Students' Learning Outcomes in Chemistry
citation: Adesoji, F. A., & Idika, M. I. (2015). Effects of 7E learning cycle model and case-based learning strategy on secondary school students' learning outcomes in chemistry. Journal of International Society for Teacher Education, 19(1). https://jiste.org/
title: 7E learning cycle model
description: The 7E learning cycle is a constructivist, inquiry-based instructional model with seven phases: elicit, engage, explore, explain, elaborate, evaluate, and extend. The article describes it as helping "make for an  effective learning process through seven steps," beginning by examining learners' prior knowledge before new content and ending with explicit transfer of learning. In the study it was operationalized as a Teachers' Instructional Guide used to teach ionic theory, oxidation-reduction, mole concept, and electrolysis over four weeks.
requirements: Teachers must be trained to follow the seven steps within a reasonable timeframe
Assessment of prior knowledge (eliciting) must not be omitted
constraints: The article reports it is more complex, somewhat 'alien,' and requires more class-time and teacher expertise than case-based learning
examples: Experimental classes were taught with a Teachers' Instructional Guide for 7E Learning Cycle Model for four weeks after one week of teacher training
key_sources: Adesoji, F. A., & Idika, M. I. (2015). Effects of 7E learning cycle model and case-based learning strategy on secondary school students' learning outcomes in chemistry. Journal of International Society for Teacher Education, 19(1). https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1177065

article_title: Effect of Multimedia Assisted 7e Learning Model Applications on Academic Achievement and Retention in Students
citation: Sarac, H., & Tarhan, D. (2017). Effect of multimedia assisted 7e learning model applications on academic achievement and retention in students. European Journal of Educational Research, 6(3), 299-311. https://doi.org/10.12973/eu-jer.6.3.299
title: 7E learning model as a constructivist instructional sequence for science teaching
description: The 7E learning model is a constructivist, inquiry-based instructional sequence for science teaching, described as an improved version of the 5E model developed by Eisenkraft. The article states its stages as "elicit, engage, explore, explain, elaborate, evaluate, and extend". In this study, multimedia materials (pictures, activity drawings, animations, simulations, video-films) were prepared for each stage of the model and used to teach the fifth-grade Matter's Change Unit.
requirements: Instructional materials prepared for each stage of the 7E model
A constructivist, research-inquiry based learning orientation in the curriculum
constraints: The article evaluates the model only in combination with multimedia-supported materials in a fifth-grade science unit
target_learning_goals: science academic achievement in the Matter's Change Unit
examples: Experimental groups were taught with multimedia materials prepared according to the 7E model stages over 20 lesson hours across five weeks, while control groups received traditional lecture-based teaching.
key_sources: Sarac, H., & Tarhan, D. (2017). Effect of multimedia assisted 7e learning model applications on academic achievement and retention in students. European Journal of Educational Research, 6(3), 299-311. https://doi.org/10.12973/eu-jer.6.3.299

article_title: The value of the '7E' instructional model in the teaching of nursing students in nursing clinical probation.
citation: Cui Liping, Dong Yuting, Zhang Shan, Shi Xiaoxia. (2024). The value of the ‘7E’ instructional model in the teaching of nursing students in nursing clinical probation. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-06157-9
title: 7E instructional model: a constructivist seven-stage learning cycle adding elicit and extend to the 5E model
description: The 7E instructional model is "based on the theory of constructivism" and was proposed in 2003 by Arthur Einsenkraft, who built on the 5E model and "added the two new stages of 'elicit' and 'extend'". Its seven stages are elicit, engage, explore, explain, elaborate, evaluate and extend. The article describes it as "systematic, cyclical, extensive and practical", enabling diverse teaching methods at each stage and encouraging inquiry-based learning that extends knowledge to multidisciplinary fields. In this study it was implemented in surgical-nursing clinical probation.
requirements: Teaching syllabus requirements consistent across compared conditions; stages run in an orderly sequence over repeated sessions
constraints: The article notes few studies apply the model in nursing teaching and its effect "needs further verification"
target_learners: junior nursing undergraduates on clinical probation
examples: In the experimental group each stage was instantiated with real clinical cases, CBL–RISE case discussion, student-designed simulation scripts, weighted evaluate assessments, and an extend stage built around parallel medical records and narrative nursing
key_sources: Cui Liping, Dong Yuting, Zhang Shan, Shi Xiaoxia. (2024). The value of the ‘7E’ instructional model in the teaching of nursing students in nursing clinical probation. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-06157-9

article_title: The value of the '7E' instructional model in the teaching of nursing students in nursing clinical probation.
citation: Cui Liping, Dong Yuting, Zhang Shan, Shi Xiaoxia. (2024). The value of the ‘7E’ instructional model in the teaching of nursing students in nursing clinical probation. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-06157-9
title: 7E-based clinical probation lesson structure combining case-based exploration, student-designed simulation, weighted evaluation and parallel-medical-record extension
description: A recurring unit-level instructional design in which each probation lesson runs through the seven 7E stages: pre-class elicitation materials, engagement with the clinical case, CBL–RISE group case discussion at the explore stage, cross-group comparison and instructor concept formation at the explain stage, student-authored simulation scripts presented in three phases ("preparation, implementation planning and evaluation"), a weighted evaluate stage (theory 60%, skills 40%), and an extend stage of six sessions built around narrative-nursing literature, film, writing and sharing of parallel medical records via PBL. Sessions ran twice weekly for "≥ 120 min each time, and a total of 24 lessons were taught".
requirements: Online platform for pre-class release of cases, literature and reference materials; instructor availability for prompts and peer-evaluation guidance
constraints: The article recommends the model for probation teaching sessions and states the study covered only clinical probation teaching
target_learners: junior nursing undergraduates on clinical probation
target_learning_goals: integration of theory with clinical practice
examples: Extend-stage sessions included watching narrative nursing practice videos, instructor-led writing skills instruction, and post-class parallel medical record completion in two sessions, shared via PBL group discussion or peer sharing by internship-stage students
key_sources: Cui Liping, Dong Yuting, Zhang Shan, Shi Xiaoxia. (2024). The value of the ‘7E’ instructional model in the teaching of nursing students in nursing clinical probation. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-06157-9
